title: Point-Free Obscurity
pattern: Developers eliminate all intermediate variables and compile functions strictly through a chain of higher-order function compositions, lambdas, or combinators.
why_bad: Locally, the code looks highly "concise" and elegant to functional programming purists. Globally, it destroys code readability and debuggability. The human mind can only process a limited number of quanta in working memory (4-7 discrete elements). Eliminating named variables strips the code of self-documenting semantic anchors, forcing maintainers to mentally execute the type checker to understand the data flow. When a runtime error occurs, the stack traces are often highly nested and virtually incomprehensible.
detection: A chain of multiple generic functional compositions (`compose`, `pipe`, `and_then`) where there are no local variable bindings or named parameters to identify intermediate states.
counterexample: Short, simple iterator pipelines (e.g., `vec.iter().map(|x| x + 1).collect()`) are idiomatic and clean. Mark `Context-dependent`.
source: Eric Elliott, *Composing Software*, "Working Memory" (p. 95) / Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* "Complexity is determined by activities..." (p. 25).
